spatialBenefitAssessment: Promising and worth revision. The two independently selectable aggregation seams expose version-only and operation-only results (both 4%) before the intersection (40%), whereas the recommended video jumps from pooled evidence to version-filtered exports. Area times height is a meaningful spatial encoding rather than arbitrary concealment. It must accurately communicate aggregation of a fixed dataset, preserve its volume claim and remain legible without decorative apparatus.

findings.issue: The geometry redistributes amber into healthy subgroups when joined, but captions describe failures as physically spread across v2. This can imply changing which requests failed.
findings.requestedChange: Describe the amber layer as the current aggregate rate representation, with fixed underlying failures. Change the version-only sentence to explain that healthy v2 operations dilute the export result. Put the mapping in one concise caption: footprint = requests, height = error rate, same 40 failures. Keep the four fixture counts unchanged in every state.
findings.evidence: interaction.js heights() assigns each joined subgroup the same aggregate height despite FAILED being zero for three groups; describe() says failures are still spread across v2. Guide example fixes all 40 failures in v2 exports.

findings.issue: Decorative combs and unlabeled gauges consume the front edges while the causal scale and 100-request cell meaning are absent from the visible explanation.
findings.requestedChange: Remove Router_* and Operation_* comb geometry. Retain one clear 0/40/100% gauge next to the v2 export column, move it so it does not cover the amber face, and identify one top cell as 100 requests with a short engraved legend. Reframe for the split states and improve grid contrast without adding floating cards.
findings.evidence: initial.png shows a large pale block, barely visible grid/amber hairline and two rows of black teeth. poster.png places the gauge directly in front of the narrow amber column. build_scene.py calls the combs router/operation proportions; intent acknowledges they are decorative.

findings.issue: The claimed conserved amber volume is only approximate in the authored geometry.
findings.requestedChange: Use exact proportional footprints for the failure meshes, or qualify the conservation claim as approximate. Separate visual outlines from measured volume so seam gaps and amber lips do not change the quantity being taught.
findings.evidence: build_scene.py uses GAP=0.008 and LIP=0.012, so amber footprints exceed nominal subgroup areas by 0.008 per dimension; the relative distortion is greatest in the 0.5-by-0.5 export cell. interaction.js heights() uses ideal N ratios.

findings.issue: Repeated control input can leave concurrent tweens writing the same positions and heights.
findings.requestedChange: Cancel/replace the current aggregation tween from its current interpolated pose when either split changes, or disable both split controls until completion. Ensure the final caption belongs to the settled selection.
findings.evidence: interaction.js apply() appends animate() work on every action without a busy guard or cancellation; advance() executes every queued writer. This is a source-level risk, not a reproduced browser failure.

requiredVerification: Coordinator: capture all four split combinations at 420px and desktop; only initial.png exists as runtime evidence. The both-split poster is a separately posed Blender render.
Check both splitting orders and rapid repeated toggles, reset mid-animation and reduced motion. Confirm 40/10000, 40/1000, 40/1000, 40/100 and 0/900 in the appropriate states.
Measure rendered amber volume against footprint and rate; verify no decorative mesh intercepts block/knob picks, and both essential actions work from the keyboard.
Ask a reader to explain why either single split still dilutes the failure, using the geometry; omit if it remains only a harder-to-read bar chart.
